reviews.headline: Memory and optics de-gross on the CXMT and Hock Tan headlines while money rotates into hyperscalers; ASML, TSMC and Anthropic's investor day are the next tests.

ASML's margin beat meets a demanding buy-side bar while AI de-grossing rolls on into Anthropic's investor day; semis and memory money keeps rotating into Mag 7 cloud names, where GS PB now sees HF exposure at highs.

The AI trade's marginal variable is now credit, not demand: CoreWeave's 15% yield and an Anthropic Q3 without an ARR number drove the sixth-to-seventh straight SOX down day, Korea hit circuit breakers as the memory corporate bid disappeared, and TSMC's 'demand exceeds supply' print was judged against a beat-and-raise bar it did not clear on margins.

Positioning flushed, credit still the swing factor: PB data show long liquidation in semis and hyperscalers (memory already de-crowded), Jensen's CoreWeave defence bought a bounce but not a credit repair, and the squeeze moved to crowded software and internet shorts.

Into the first megacap prints the desks are long META and AMZN, short-ish GOOGL, and the CoreWeave trade is attracting its first long-only tourists while memory and semicap stay split between HF bears and LO bulls.

Weekend mail is about the mechanism, not the thesis: the largest tech sell skew in five years was hedge-fund de-grossing, semicap and Korea are where holders are least sure, and Apple, Mag7 and software are where the money hid.

Monday's bounce is a SemiAnalysis headline and a CoreWeave upgrade landing on a tape that just set a record for net selling of Info Tech; the desks still cannot name the clearing event, and the crowding has migrated into TXN, LRCX, WDC, META and MSFT while memory, HDDs and neoclouds trade on technicals.

Monday's SOX bounce had no sponsors (HFs the largest share of Jefferies' tech flow in two years, JPM's desk 'not seeing any real demand'), CoreWeave could not hold an upgrade, Elice's -32% Korean neocloud debut and SoftBank's 4-year-high CDS re-opened the funding wound, and the crowding is now explicit: long AMZN, META, TXN and APH, short NFLX, TEL and Ciena, with GOOGL and NVDA the new homes of the Mag 7 short book.

META.summary: Bernstein's Shmulik reiterates Outperform ($800) but leans cautious into the print on valuation and a high bar; FY26-27 EPS come down meaningfully for higher opex, capex and the $10B legal settlement; he is hesitant to underwrite Muse retention too soon.

COHR.summary: Bernstein's Zhu leans positive on COHR (4 Nov) after a -28% month on a non-fundamental AI drawdown: above consensus on Q1 revenue ($2.4B vs $2.3B) and EPS, potential to guide up; the long-term debate is bandwidth-driven 2028+ upside vs reliance on InP-constrained economics.

LITE.summary: Bernstein's Zhu is in line with consensus for LITE's quarter (5 Nov) with more Q2 upside, expecting focus on the $40 2028 EPS guide and the OCS debate; Jefferies' OCP recap separately names LITE and MTSI as most levered to 1.6T (80M units in C27) with NPO leading scale-up through C28.

NOW.summary: Bernstein's Peter Weed stays bullish into NOW's Q3 (Outperform, PT $266): checks show AI-native SKU adoption ~50% at renewal and 80%+ of recent contracts include AI, adding ~60-70bps in Q4 and 1.5-2pts at peak, supporting ~20% growth through FY28; JPM (Chatterjee) also 'remains favorable' on strong partner checks.

AAPL.summary: Loop Capital downgrades AAPL to Hold (PT $330 from $370): the ~10% Sep/Dec iPhone shipment cuts now look demand-driven rather than purely supply, memory costs add gross-margin risk; the downgrade was also listed by Barclays Rand, UBS Ruple and GS Kamshad.

SKHYNIX.summary: JPM (Kwon) memory update as relayed by TMTB: the top three memory shares are down ~42% from peak and price a 2027 downcycle that spot DRAM (flat-to-up), HBM ASP negotiations (biased higher) and order talks into 2028/29 do not support; preference SK Hynix over Samsung, capital returns the cleanest catalyst.

ORCL.summary: Into the 28 Oct investor day: JPM expects an FY30 target raise but says funding matters more (after the $20B ATM Oracle still needs ~$20B more in FY27, gross capex $90-95B; confirmation of a FY27/28 capex peak the cleanest catalyst); Citi sees LT targets rising on $200B+ net new RPO; BofA's Liani publishes a wish list on financing and RPO composition.

SAMSUNG.summary: KB's Jeff Kim (via Jefferies Asia TMT): ~80% of Samsung's 2027 memory output is secured by LTAs (5-year deals on 70% of conventional, annual contracts on 100% of HBM), HBM ASPs +100-150% y/y in 2027 vs investor expectations of ~70% (likely Samsung HBM4-specific), Samsung HBM share to 80%.

MSFT.summary: Schilsky: after +37% since the last print, investor sentiment on MSFT is 'VERY high' (it was a funding short a quarter ago); bogeys Azure +46-47% cc with a bias high, Q2 guide calling for acceleration, Copilot seat adds high-single-digit millions (+10m better), FY27 capex $210-230B vs Street ~$190B.

SHOP.summary: JPM's Smilek Platinum Partner call (Zettler): AI channels drive ~2-3% of merchant traffic and GMV today and could reach 10%+ in 1-2 years; Sidekick engagement improving and SHOP's enterprise push viewed constructively.

LRCX.summary: UBS technicals: AMAT, KLAC, LRCX and SK Hynix are on absolute underperformance streaks (down at least 9 of the last 10 sessions) and the same four are relative underperformers vs SPY; CRWV and UCTT screen RSI-oversold.

CRWD.summary: UBS's Boyd (previewing TENB/QLYS/RPD, all Neutral): partner checks say CrowdStrike EM benefits from the platform effect, with endpoint-first VM offerings taking incremental demand; he models CRWD Exposure Management surpassing $400M ARR in 2Q and ~40% of industry NNARR over the TTM.

SPCX.summary: Favuzza: the SPCX implied earnings move 'feels a bit too low' given a 14% absolute move last quarter, a 4.8 beta on a tiny sample and still-wide buy-side expectations post IPO.

TXN.summary: Favuzza on implied moves: TXN carries ~100bps more implied move than LRCX, odd for an analog versus the most expensive, highest-beta semicap, echoing the ACN-vs-MU week.

CRWV.summary: Favuzza: popular inbound was 'this CRWV move, aka can't rally on an upgrade, shows that we aren't out of the woods yet right?'; separately HFs were the largest share of Jefferies tech flow in two years on Monday, pointing to frozen duration investors waiting for catalysts.

SNOW.summary: Jefferies' two SNOW CoCo customer calls (Thill): CoCo could lift consumption 10-30% via faster builds and agent compute, the moat sits in the governed data/context layer, pipeline healthy but not yet inflecting, CoWork adoption early.

CRM.summary: Favuzza/Wong: Salesforce agrees to buy Braze for $47.50 cash (~58% premium, $5.66bn, ~5x CY27 sales), CRM -3% pre-market while SMID software (HUBS, KVYO) rallies; no change to FY27 guidance and FY28 not guided.

RDDT.summary: Favuzza: JC's preview is fairly cautious with the print hinging on US DAUs; early buy-side conversations point to FQ3 revenue ~$935M vs guide $860-870M and a Q4 guide ~$1.08B vs Street $1.05B, with US DAUs 'must grow, but +0.2M q/q should be good enough'.

houses: Rothschild & Co Redburn (AI Financing call, Capstone notes)
NVDA.summary: GS desk: NVDA led the most-active high-touch list (with CRWV, WDC, CMCSA, AMZN) on Monday; Tuesday pre-market the AI trade is back under pressure (SMH -1%, DRAM -4%, CRWV/NBIS -5%) on Elice and capital/credit worries, while Reuters reports ByteDance/Alibaba/Tencent ordered >$35B of RTX PRO 5500 that NVDA cannot guarantee to fill.

PLTR.summary: Jefferies software into prints (Thill via Beavington): PLTR stays Underperform with standout execution but consensus above the guide and a full valuation; DT is the top pick, TEAM and PCOR liked, DDOG a Hold; internet and software preferred as a hedge to an AI unwind.

KIOXIA.summary: BofA Japan (Hirakawa, via Franco's one-liners): North American investors are bullish on the memory cycle and Kioxia on valuation; WFE outlook broadly bullish but with concerns over supply constraints and a 2029 slowdown.

GEV.summary: BofA's Obin (Buy, PO $1,310) previews GEV 3Q with $21.0bn of orders (1.70x book-to-bill, +44% y/y) including 13GW of gas power equipment contracts; Vertiv's preview is titled 'getting over last quarter's speed bump'.

NFLX.summary: Dwyer: NFLX 'remains a very crowded short' among faster money into tonight's print; engagement is the overhang and the UCAN growth algorithm into 2027 the debate; a fair amount of air is out of expectations, but nobody races to be first through the door; bogeys 12% USD revenue, 33.2% OM, 4Q growth 11% vs Street 12%.

AVGO.summary: Same Barclays desk read applied to AVGO: more investors shifting long NVDA/AVGO as the lower-valuation, lower-beta way to stay in compute while cautious on the space; AVGO screens RSI 39 on the desk's list.

APH.summary: Barclays' Hardwick (via Rand): APH investors are still very positively positioned; optics/copper is no longer the first question and the ~60% of sales outside IT Datacom now gets asked about; a Q3 beat and above-consensus Q4 guide are expected but expectations are lower than before Q2.

TEL.summary: Hardwick (via Rand): pushing TEL as an OW idea has been 'tough sledding' in a month of marketing, with interest only from value and activist investors; HFs clearly favour APH and view TEL as the likely pair short until it delivers on DDN and a few good quarters.

WDC.summary: Rand: outside analog, optical and HDDs sit near the top of preferred long spaces into prints; WDC was also on GS's most-active high-touch list Monday after the storage-led bounce (WDC +6%); Arcuri flags WDC among the three most-watched prints this week.

SMCI.summary: Barclays streaks: SMCI is on an 8-day relative underperformance streak vs SMH, with AMKR, HPE, LITE, MKSI, FLEX, FN, AEIS and DELL/SANM also lagging; CRWV, FN and APLD printed 52-week lows.

DDOG.summary: Rand: investors will remain long DDOG (and SNOW) into prints despite high expectations; Jefferies' Beavington notes Thill stays sidelined on DDOG (Hold, +82% YTD, largest customer steps down in Q3) preferring SNOW, a divergence from Bernstein's Monday upgrade.

MDB.summary: Rand: investors want to see good prints or commentary before getting more involved on the long side in MDB, DT and ESTC; Jefferies lists DT as its software top pick into prints.

PANW.summary: Rand on security: investors still like the theme but worry valuations have run on 'Mythos' concerns while the numbers impact is far smaller, a high bar with downside risk and positioning likely to shift more cautious into prints; CRWD, AKAM, PANW, NET and FTNT are on 5-6 day relative underperformance streaks vs IGV.

DELL.summary: Michael Dell (WSJ interview, via TMTB podcast brief; also relayed by MS Wigg): the DRAM shortage likely worsens in 2027 since fabs under construction do not produce until 2029, 'maybe a four-year problem'; enterprise AI factory customer adds accelerated ~2.75x (3,300 in three quarters vs 3,200 in eight).

AMZN.summary: Business Insider recording/documents (relayed by Rothschild, UBS Dwyer and Jefferies Wong, one claim): AWS CFO Felton told infra chief Kalyanaraman 'you've taken us free cash flow negative', FCF negative 'the next couple of years', ~$5bn of GB300 racks in August then ~$3bn a month with some racks warehoused for lack of power; AWS still expects demand to exceed capacity in 2027.

MU.summary: Micron's Taoyuan union plans a Thursday strike amid bonus mediation in Taichung (Taiwan ~15,000 staff, HBM); Redburn's view is no major impact on AI server shipments unless prolonged; MU -2.6% pre-market per Jefferies.

KLAC.summary: Jefferies semicap recap of SEMICON West: cleanroom space then the supply base are the constraints to ~$300B WFE by C28, pricing is firming and visibility runs 3-4 quarters; the group is out of favour but KLAC is liked as business should begin to accelerate.

ASML.summary: Beavington's chart: the AI chip trade is bifurcating, with revisions up since June for NVDA, AMD and ASML and down for Micron, SK Hynix and CoreWeave, leaving the cyclical cohort needing fresh catalysts; Asian semis fell on SoftBank's CDS (432bp, 4-year high).

CRDO.summary: Jefferies OCP recap: CRDO had 'perhaps the most incremental content at the show' (micro-VCSEL ALC, NVDA qualification of 800G ZF optics, an optical backplane with SENKO); NPO leads the scale-up design cycle through C27-C28 with meaningful CPO pushed to C29.

SNPS.summary: MS raises SNPS PT to $574 (Overweight): the market still undervalues the AI revenue opportunity, with the stock on 25x FY27 EPS despite +18% in a month vs a 36x five-year average; Barclays' desk lists SNPS on a 6-day negative streak and Bloomberg-X attention is falling (Δz -1.3).

CDNS.summary: MS (Overweight, PT $400) sets a high bar for CDNS into 26 Oct: strong numbers are not enough, management must connect AI adoption to incremental earnings; no Synopsys-style headline AI partnership expected, but broad adoption of Cadence tools among AI developers.

STX.summary: TMTB on the HDD bounce (STX +3.4%, WDC +6%): TrendForce has HDD lead times at 50 weeks vs 16 balanced with hyperscalers locking 2028 supply; bulls say nearline exabytes are allocated into CY29 with pricing contracted through CY27/28, bears cite UBS's STX note that TDK heads and Toshiba capacity break the 'no new capacity' narrative into a late-2028/early-2029 downcycle.

NBIS.summary: Redburn's new Sell on Nebius sees c60% downside (CoreWeave c33%) on the same neolab-demand argument; Nebius was +3% on Monday while CRWV faded and -5% pre-market Tuesday on Elice.

GOOG.summary: Schilsky: GOOGL is the Battleground, Search expected to miss by ~100bps on alt data while Cloud crushes on TPUs (investors +105-115%, implied TPU sales $5-7B, revenue/GW heard from $10B to $35B); Cloud margin vs ~33% is the 'sneaky most important KPI'; 2027 capex expectations $330-350B vs Street ~$305B.

AMAT.summary: Arcuri found AMAT's SEMICON presentation weak: a model gaining only 10bps of WFE share over four years (LRCX and KLAC gain more) was 'either massively sandbagged or out of touch', 54% GM not exciting; at 13x the stock embeds something below $300bn 2028 WFE, and he likes it mainly for the DRAM mix shift.

AMD.summary: Arcuri: AMD's business is great and TSMC is 'bending over backwards' on allocation; his server number is more than double guide (~$40bn next year); expectations-wise investors are already there, with EPS >$30 and $35-40 in a minority of conversations; Harlan Sur (via JPM See) also flags AMD, TXN and INTC as 3Q positive-surprise candidates.

INTC.summary: Arcuri: INTC should beat September on GM/revenue and sandbag December, but the key debate is TSMC's frustration with INTC's EMIB-T engagement curtailing wafer allocation, forcing much higher INTC capex; narrative good, valuation hard, with <$7-8 of 2030 earnings.

TSM.summary: Arcuri's SEMICON read-through for TSMC: Terafab ($5bn WFE next year, $10bn in 2028, possibly low) is a very disruptive continuous-flow fab concept with implications for TSMC and INTC, and TSMC is 'upset' about the engagement INTC gets on EMIB-T, which may cost INTC wafer allocation next year.

TER.summary: Arcuri: TER and Advantest both sounded 'incredibly bullish' at SEMICON, one citing a doubling of tester production from 2H26 to 2H28 vs Tim's +80% revenue, implying upside; TER optimistic AMZN is up a lot next year on complexity/units and GOOGL could become bigger than AMZN; 'TER at $340 is attractive'.

ADVANTEST.summary: Same Arcuri claim applied to Advantest: both test leaders 'incredibly bullish', with a doubling of tester production 2H26 to 2H28 cited; MS's Shane Brett separately models test at 8.5% of WFE in 2026 vs 5.8% in 2020-24 and questions how far intensity can rise.

MRVL.summary: Arcuri likes MRVL a lot on networking and Maia: Hock expects networking's share of AI revenue to rise from ~30%, Tim sees a major networking inflection, and MRVL pivoted investors back to its networking franchise at the analyst day.

CIEN.summary: Beavington: many US investors have been long Nokia and short Ciena (Nokia seen gaining share and cheaper), which explains Ciena's pressure; he sees both doing very well with little difference in optical; a Nokia guidance raise is a consensus 'when, not if' with HFs waiting to buy after Q3.

BESI.summary: Silver: BESI is the tactical debate into Thursday, a squeeze set-up if earnings surprise against a challenged hybrid-bonding/HBM narrative; sentiment has deteriorated meaningfully, hedge funds have seemingly been short for some time and the long-only dip-buying base is less certain this time.

GLW.summary: Wamsi Mohan previews a GLW beat-and-raise on AI optical (Q3 revs $5.04B/EPS $0.89, optical $2.23B +7.8% QoQ, Q4 guide $5.3B), with near-term upside limited by capacity commissioning timing.

SPOT.summary: Fenske: SPOT's Q4 gross-margin message is 'the most televised' after conferences and CFO meetings, likely lighter than historical expansion on Reserved/Fitness spend; the bigger picture is AI products not yet launched pending label deals; buy-side Q3 premium adds 5.67M vs Street 5.1M.

WOLF.summary: Digitimes (via Wigg): IFX extends its WOLF wafer deal to 8-inch silicon carbide; WOLF's Bloomberg-X attention is nonetheless falling fast (Δz -3.2) after last week's rally faded.

NVTS.summary: Blayne Curtis from OCP: 800V power was a common theme and NVTS's collaborations with NVDA and MCHP put it in front of customers ahead of the 2027-28 design cycle.

SMTC.summary: Blayne expects NPO to dominate the scale-up optical design cycle through 2027-28 with meaningful CPO adoption pushed to 2029 or later, a content uplift for MTSI and SMTC; NVDA's USFP and CSCO/ANET XPO designs suggest pluggables are more durable than investors expect.

TSLA.summary: TSLA is on UBS's list of HF crowded longs where mutual funds are underweight, into the 21 Oct print; no other desk mail in the window discussed the name.

CEG.summary: UBS derivatives: within AI, investors rotated into hyperscalers and quality is +10% MTD vs momentum -10%; Romano's preferred AI expression is the AI Power basket (UBXXVOLT) where positioning is cleanest after power dislocated from XLU on AI funding fears. Basket constituents are not listed in the mail; CEG is used here as the power proxy the wiki tracks.

ANET.summary: Vogt sees broader hyperscaler demand beyond Meta and Microsoft lifting ANET's September quarter above estimates and consensus, with conservative initial CY27 growth guidance of 25-30%.

MEDIATEK.summary: Against TPU v9 slip worries, UBS's Sunny Lin sees the 30 Oct call as a positive catalyst: v8t shipments on track for Q4 sales +27% QoQ, operating margin 15% to 18.5% to 25-26% in 2027, and a v9 tape-out delay that does not shift the multi-year opportunity (Key Call Buy).

VRT.summary: JPM's new industrials analyst Julian Mitchell argues we are quite far into the AI capex cycle and the macro feels late-cycle; generalists are more circumspect, there is 'very little consensus' in his AI coverage (low dispersion across GEV, ETN, VRT) and data-centre equipment margins could normalise lower once volume growth slows.

APP.summary: Same Schilsky read: APP's +7% squeeze marks it among the most crowded shorts, which sits against UBS's report of renewed long interest in the name.

SNDK.summary: At OCP, Hynix spent much of its talk on high-bandwidth flash (about half HBM bandwidth at 14x the capacity), which MS reads as significant upside optionality for Sandisk, which has also emphasised the standard.

ARM.summary: Asian investors are upbeat on agentic CPU demand but picked up concern that the move in CPU stocks (AMD, ARM, INTC, QCOM) has been narrative-driven and could disappoint near term.

QCOM.summary: Qualcomm's hyperscaler opportunities in the US and China are each tracking well above $1bn with AWS a 2027+ contributor; the accelerator lead is real but early.

UBER.summary: From a week of internet marketing: the consensus shorts are UBER, NFLX and EXPE, while longs are happy owning ABNB, U, TTWO and DASH.

DT.summary: Thill favors DT in observability's agent wave, aided by Arize and ARR converging with 20%+ consumption growth; Buy, PT to $75.

PWR.summary: From Data Center World Expo Singapore: experts expect DC demand to accelerate in 2027, supply chain is the constraint, prefab/modular prioritized and the industry is converging on 800VDC with 2027-2029 deployment; read positive for PWR (grid), CAT and CMI; investors now ask which industrials carry neocloud vs hyperscaler exposure after the CoreWeave bonds.

ADI.summary: On Arcuri's bus tour (NVDA, MU, ADI plus a data-center developer dinner) all three managements were bullish and ADI was the most incrementally bullish.

BKNG.summary: Jefferies' internet team pitches internet names as a hedge to an AI unwind (strong negative correlation with semis, fundamentals insulated from AI disintermediation) and names BKNG, EXPE and Z as the most likely beneficiaries of waning AI enthusiasm.

ON.summary: DB's distributor scrape shows mature-node tightness intensifying in October: onsemi pushed a 10-20% price increase effective 10 Oct, power-discrete lead times are 40-52 weeks and SiC MOSFET demand is picking up.

ALAB.summary: Jefferies: Astera's Aries 7 adds optical drivers and TIAs (first optical entry), multiple NPO designs on micro-VCSEL and UHP, and the Orion rack (80 GPUs, 12 Scorpio X switches) targets enterprise inference and neoclouds.

AIXA.summary: Jefferies EU desk: Aixtron pre-announced 3Q26 orders 30% ahead of consensus at EUR 275m, driven by InP tool demand from optical supply-chain tightness.

HPE.summary: Barclays research also downgrades HPE to Equal Weight after a ~186% YTD run, seeing less upside in servers and storage as memory prices normalise.

TOKYOELEC.summary: Jefferies Asia desk doubts CXMT's 4F2 is commercial yet, but from a recent Japan trip it reports TEL, Daifuku and Kokusai all seeing aggressive CXMT order ramps.

NXPI.summary: The Bernstein bus-tour relay is broadly constructive on demand. Intel margin/cost and substrate challenges, Nvidia financing/returns, Broadcom customer engagement and NXPI/AMAT growth need to be evaluated separately from stock positioning.

CSCO.summary: Campus refresh and AI demand are intact, but margin headwinds constrain the stock narrative.

IFX.summary: The specialist sees oversold analog/auto opportunities despite prevailing apathy; oversold is an opinion, not a measurement of investor underownership.

AGX.summary: The construction conference recap includes Argan within strong multi-year end markets, with execution, labor and prefab as margin drivers. It provides no Argan-specific investor-positioning evidence.

TLN.summary: The PJM procurement discussion identifies Talen as a possible participant after large projects absorb some capacity need. This is a scenario, not a disclosed award or crowded-stock signal.

VST.summary: Investors want more buybacks following the financing transaction cited in the weekly power recap. No direction or size of equity flows is given.

BE.summary: The power-sector recap characterizes Oracle commentary as cautious for Bloom Energy. The short excerpt is a read-through, not a full desk thesis or ownership observation.

TSEM.summary: The initiation favors architecture-agnostic silicon-photonics exposure. Strong demand visibility is balanced by future competition and pricing risk; no client positioning is supplied.

ESTC.summary: Lenschow returns from management meetings more confident in security adoption, search/GenAI and the medium-term growth path. This is research conviction, not observed ownership.

NVT.summary: Hawney identifies nVent as a preferred US AI/electrification exposure while seeing a less stretched sector setup. No nVent-specific position size is supplied.

DISCO.summary: The relayed phrase calls Disco a funding name while citing low valuation for long-term investors. Its direction is ambiguous; no long/short label is imposed.

OKTA.summary: Seidman reports more short discussions alongside Bernstein research downgrades: valuation and a high growth bar, rather than collapsing demand, drive the caution.

FLEX.summary: The Axiom filing reveals higher customer concentration than expected and differing segment economics. Positive power growth should be weighed against this concentration risk.

NET.summary: Callahan finds few fundamental bears; the debate is valuation and the durability of reacceleration, with traffic and agentic monetization supporting the bull case.

SMIC.summary: Tokyo Electron meeting notes describe increasing SMIC/Hua Hong investment. This is a supplier read-through, not evidence of SMIC investor sentiment or ownership.

SANM.summary: Sanmina is included in positive Rising Tech Leaders conference commentary. The excerpt supports constructive management tone, but is insufficient to assign stock-specific crowding.

WMB.summary: Williams appears among the team’s fall top ideas. The sector backdrop still includes affordability and refinancing risks; the excerpt contains no stock-specific crowding measure.

AKAM.summary: The bull case is inexpensive edge inference and attractive steady-state contracts; the overhang is incremental capex and unclear near-term unit economics.

AEIS.summary: AEIS is included in Brett’s preferred equipment names. A preference alone does not establish crowding or new client demand.

MCHP.summary: Microchip is included in Sur’s preferred industrial-analog group. This is research selection, not observed investor buying or ownership.

observations.author: William Beavington
observations.summary: Jefferies' clients push back on the CXMT 4F2 scare: no samples in the supply chain, no ramp timeline, and CXMT's proposed 4F2 cell at F=15nm (900nm2) is still no denser than the Koreans/Micron at 6F2 and 12.2nm (893nm2); 2028 is the realistic timeframe.
observations.excerpt: So CXMT’s proposed cell size will still not be as dense as Korean/MU’s current cell size. At the same size, with advanced EUV lithography, the Koreans/MU will get to F value of 8nm which will translate into cell size of 384 nm^2, while still staying at 6F^2 with great yields.
